newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end weaker, at lows in technial trade.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end weaker, at lows in technial trade.

text.p: FCOJ futures settled weaker and at the day's lows amid technically inspired fund selling, floor sources said.
Short-covering by the trade stymied losses until the close, when the trade became a seller, pressuring the most-active July contract closer to its downside target of 77.80 cents, dealers said.

The contract settled down 1.60 cents at 78.25 cents per lb, having ranged from 80.20 to 78.25 cents. Second-position September closed 1.70 weaker at 80.50 cents, while the rest of the board finished 1.20 to 2.30 lower.
"The selloff today is a continuation of what we have had over the past few days," Dean Witter vice president Celeste Gerogakis, said.

She blamed losses on a combination of fundamental and technical factors. Early selling pushed July through nearby support at 80.00 cents, triggering stops and pushing the contract to the day's low of 78.25 cents.
Traders expect early selling on Thursday to trigger stops waiting just below 78.00 cents. "The market is not oversold yet," Georgakis said.
Fundamentally, burgeoning world supplies and slack demand should continue to weigh on the market, analysts said.
An estimated 3,500 lots changed hands on the day, compared with Tuesday's official 2,747 lots.
